24 A person stands at the side of a straight railway track. A train moves towards the person and
emits sound from its whistle. The person hears a sound of frequency 1690 Hz as the train
approaches him.
The person then hears sound of frequency 1500 Hz as the train moves away from him. The
speed of sound in air is 340 m s–1.
What is the speed of the train?
A
20 m s–1
B
38 m s–1
C
41 m s–1
D
43 m s–1

hints: Notice you have two observed frequencies, $1690 \text{ Hz}$ approaching and $1500 \text{ Hz}$ receding, but the true whistle frequency is not given.
Recall the Doppler shift shortens the wavelength on approach with $v - v_s$ and stretches it on recession with $v + v_s$, with $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Divide the two Doppler equations to cancel the unknown source frequency, then solve the ratio $1690/1500 = (340+v_s)/(340-v_s)$ for $v_s$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: observed $f_a = 1690 \text{ Hz}$ on approach, $f_r = 1500 \text{ Hz}$ on recession, wave speed $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, train speed $v_s$ and source frequency $f_0$ unknown.
State the Doppler rule for a moving source and stationary observer: $f_a = f_0 v/(v - v_s)$ and $f_r = f_0 v/(v + v_s)$.
Eliminate $f_0$ by dividing: $f_a/f_r = (v + v_s)/(v - v_s)$, so $1690/1500 = (340 + v_s)/(340 - v_s)$.
Check units are $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and round sensibly to $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Dividing the approaching and receding Doppler equations eliminates the unknown whistle frequency and gives $v_s \approx 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This is too large and does not satisfy the observed ratio $1690/1500$ when substituted into $(v+v_s)/(v-v_s)$.

C.explanation: This is too large; it would give a much larger shift between the $1690 \text{ Hz}$ and $1500 \text{ Hz}$ frequencies than observed.

D.explanation: This is too large; it would make the approaching frequency much higher relative to the receding frequency.
